name: Bui Vien Walking Street
kicker: The night street at Phạm Ngũ Lão
summary: Night street of about 850 metres: walk the bars, stalls, and crowd where Bùi Viện crosses Phạm Ngũ Lão. It was branded the city’s second official walking street in 2017, with vehicles banned. Dinner through the night is the hour. Bánh mì, phở bò, and seafood are the plates named on the street.

notice.title: This is the night street
notice.body: Nguyễn Huệ is the sundown paving from City Hall to the river. Bùi Viện is the later street, about 850 metres, crossing Đề Thám, Phạm Ngũ Lão, and Đỗ Quang Đẩu.

body: Bùi Viện runs about 850 metres through the western quarter in District 1, crossing Đề Thám, Phạm Ngũ Lão, and Đỗ Quang Đẩu. It was branded the city’s second official walking street in 2017, and vehicles were banned. The hour is dinner through the night, and the quarter is known as a street that keeps going.

Bars, cafes, live music, and food stalls fill the walk. The plates named on it are bánh mì, phở bò, and seafood, plus barbecue. The photograph is the crowd in the roadway after dark. The second frame is the same street with the tables out under the signs. Nguyễn Huệ is the other walking street, earlier in the evening.

figures.caption: Tables along Bùi Viện, with the street still full after dark

gettingThere: If your room is on Phạm Ngũ Lão, you walk onto the street. From the cathedral square or Nguyễn Huệ it is a short ride. Minutes were not printed.

legs.heading: From Phạm Ngũ Lão
legs.body: Walk. The street crosses Phạm Ngũ Lão, Đề Thám, and Đỗ Quang Đẩu.

legs.heading: From Nguyễn Huệ
legs.body: A short ride west. The minutes were not printed. Nguyễn Huệ is the earlier walk. This one starts after dinner.

hours: After dinner through the night. A closing hour was not printed.
closed: A weekly closing day was not printed.
admissionNote: No fee for the street was printed. Food and drinks are what you buy at the tables. Check on arrival.
